notes: First Q-simple, geometrically split example of [2,12] for the census (the gsplit cell was empty). The curve is y^2 = 183(5x^2 - 17x - 37)(97x^2 - 98x - 242)(4526545x^2 - 2116653x - 4606833). Construction: quadratic-conjugate gluing over K = Q(sqrt(-11)) of the Tate normal form E: y^2 + (1 - c)xy - by = x^3 - bx^2 with c = -t(2t - 1)(3t^2 - 3t + 1)/(t - 1)^3, b = t(2t - 1)(2t^2 - 2t + 1)(3t^2 - 3t + 1)/(t - 1)^4 at t = (10 + 2*sqrt(-11))/27, where (0, 0) has order 12; found by a trace-norm search with the square conditions delta_2(z) = (z^2 + 1)(3z^2 - 1) and k_0(z) = -(z^2 - 1)(3z^2 + 1), z = 2t - 1. Exact checks: generators A = [x^2 - 98/97x - 242/97, 0] of order 2 and B of order 12 with A != 6B; #J(F_13) = 144, #J(F_19) = 336, #J(F_29) = 816 bound the torsion by 48; the three nonzero rational 2-torsion classes lie in <A, B> and A, B, A + B have no rational halves, so J(Q)_tors = [2,12]; chi_29 = T^4 - 26T^2 + 841 is irreducible, so J is simple over Q; the involution x -> (187x + 814)/(-402x - 187) of C over K has a genus-1 quotient isomorphic to E (the geometric automorphism group has order 4). J is isogenous over Q to Res_{K/Q} E, so its conductor is 11^2 * N(f_E) = 1512160026300.
